I came back to the village five years ago after working in Shijiazhuang. My university degree is in business, not agriculture, but it taught me to read fertilizer labels and calculate pure nutrient amounts myself instead of trusting whatever the input shop tells me. I farm 6 mu of wheat-maize rotation. My wife and my father both have off-farm jobs, so I manage the fields myself and hire a combine for harvest.

It is early March now, and my winter wheat — variety Jimai 32, an improved type — is greening up. Last year I applied 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer at sowing and topdressed twice with urea, totaling about 14 kg of pure nitrogen per mu. I got 480 kg per mu, but the grains were not plump enough and the protein was lower than the grade-one price threshold. This year I am raising my nitrogen target to 16 kg per mu, with 6 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium. I split it: 50 kg of 18-12-5 compound at base, then 15 kg urea at green-up and 10 kg urea at jointing. I also spread 2 cubic meters of rotted chicken manure per mu before the last rotary tillage after maize harvest — I watched my neighbor Zhang do this for three years and his soil is much darker and softer now, and his wheat roots looked stronger when I helped him dig a pit last spring. The rotary tillage costs me 40 yuan per mu but it breaks up the maize stubble and buries the manure properly. I will irrigate four times: the overwinter water is already done, plus green-up in late March, jointing in mid-April, and flowering in early May. My well pump is reliable, so water is not my main worry. For pesticides, I sprayed herbicide last autumn, and this spring I will do one fungicide at jointing for powdery mildew and one insecticide if aphids appear — three applications total for the wheat year. I expect 510 kg per mu if the spring weather holds.

For the summer maize, I will plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid right after wheat harvest in early June. I use no-tillage seeding — I pay the village cooperative 50 yuan per mu. Every day counts in June, and no-till saves me almost a week; last year my cousin tilled and he planted six days later than me, and his ears were smaller. My fertilizer plan is 18 kg pure nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I put 50 kg of 20-10-10 compound fertilizer in the seed furrow at planting, which gives me 10 kg N, 5 kg P, and 5 kg K, and then topdress 18 kg urea at the big trumpet stage for the remaining 8 kg N. I irrigate three times: at sowing if the soil is dry, at big trumpet in mid-July, and at grain filling in August. Two pesticide sprays: one post-emergence herbicide at the three-leaf stage and one insecticide for Asian corn borer at big trumpet. I budget 820 yuan per mu for all inputs on both crops. At current grain prices — wheat around 2.6 yuan per kg and maize around 2.4 yuan — my expected 510 kg wheat and 600 kg maize give me about 2,766 yuan revenue per mu, so roughly 1,946 yuan profit. That is enough to cover my part of the family expenses and still leave some for my daughter's school fees. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest — one failed crop is worse than wasting half a bag of urea.
